newsitem.title: USA: Victory funds to offer 'plain English' prospectus.
newsitem.headline: Victory funds to offer 'plain English' prospectus.

text.p: KeyCorp said its Victory Funds will begin to offer new so-called 'plain English' prospectuses starting on Wednesday.

The Victory prospectuses come in advance of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission requirement to make mutual fund companies break down the "legalese" of hard-to-read prospectuses by rewriting the cover page, summary and risk factors sections in "plain English."

The SEC approved the rule proposal on February 28, and will issue a final ruling within a year. The agency will allow 90 days for public comment after the proposal appeared in the Federal Register last week.
In part, the proposal calls for a shorter profile prospectus, as well as an overhaul of current prospectuses.
The SEC's proposed rules would make it easier for investors to understand the composition and risks of mutual funds and how those factors could affect their financial picture.
The SEC describes "plain English" as featuring short sentences with active voices as well as everyday language and easy-to-read tables.
